text:
sara (Support): Hey team — getting escalations from multiple customers about sudden spike in 5xx for streaming responses around 09:10 UTC. Customers see the stream cut off mid-chunk and in the browser they get net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET. They expect these to be client disconnects but our billing/metrics are counting them as 5xx. Ticket CS-4821. Sample req ids: req_abc123 req_def456

devon (Oncall): Thanks. Can you paste the gateway logs and an example curl/fetch repro? Also whether they use our hosted API or a proxy/extension.

sara (Support): Hosted API via browser extension (editor plugin). Pasted logs from the gateway for req_abc123: 

```
[2026-03-17T09:10:22Z] gw_id=gw-7 req=req_abc123 upstream_write_error: EPIPE while writing chunked response to downstream
[2026-03-17T09:10:22Z] gw_id=gw-7 conn=client-11 RST from 203.0.113.45:54812
[2026-03-17T09:10:22Z] gw_id=gw-7 request_end status=502 label=upstream_write_failure
```

kai (Infra): Looks like the client is sending a RST/FIN after receiving some bytes. Our gateway currently maps any write failure to upstream error and emits a 502. That means a client-initiated reset gets counted as a server 5xx. Grep across hosts shows similar pattern: 

```
# grep "upstream_write_error" /var/log/gateway/* | head
gw-3: [2026-03-17T09:09:58Z] req=req_def456 upstream_write_error: EPIPE
gw-5: [2026-03-17T09:10:01Z] req=req_ghi789 upstream_write_error: ECONNRESET
```

kai (Infra): The sequence is: response headers sent, server begins streaming chunked body, client aborts (RST). The kernel returns EPIPE/ECONNRESET on write -> gateway treats like upstream failure.

mike (SRE): Agree this inflates our 5xx counts. Two things: (1) metric classification change to distinguish downstream aborts vs real upstream failures, (2) ensure billing/usage pipeline doesn't charge retries/failed tokens for client aborts.

sara (Support): Customers are getting charged because our billing job filters by status==5xx. So if we flip heuristics they'll stop being billed incorrectly.

mike (SRE): Quick mitigation: change the gateway to classify write errors where response already had first byte sent and kernel errno is EPIPE/ECONNRESET as client_abort (non-5xx). Longer term: add labels to streaming requests: outcome={client_abort,gateway_error,upstream_error}.

devon (Oncall): I'll scope the patch. Minimal change: in streaming path, if write fails and downstream socket shows RST (tcp_info), set status_label=client_abort and return 499-like code internally. Then expose the label to metrics. ETA ~2h for canary. I'll also add a log line linking to req id and tcp flags.

support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-03-17-1 and linked CS-4821. Assigned to devon, kai.

sara (Support): Repro steps I used locally (browser):
1) Start a chunked streaming request with fetch: 
```
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams', { method: 'POST', body: promptStream, headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ...' } })
```
2) As the first chunks arrive, force-close the browser tab / kill the websocket/proxy connection (or disable network) -> client sends RST to the gateway.
3) Observe gateway logs show EPIPE and response logged as 502; metrics increment 5xx counter.

sara (Support): Also reproduces with curl: 
```
# server side: stream chunked response slowly
curl --no-buffer https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d @payload
# then kill curl (Ctrl-C) while response is mid-stream
```

kai (Infra): Good repro. Plan: patch gateway heuristics + add metric labels. Also will add a short-lived alert to watch client_abort ratio so we don't hide real server problems.

devon (Oncall): Rolling patch to gateway canary now (gw-7). Will monitor for errors and metric delta. If safe, promote cluster-wide in ~2h. I'll post results here.

sara (Support): Thanks — I'll reply to customers with the repro and ETA for fix (couple hours). Please tag me when promoted.

mike (SRE): After patch, we should run a backfill to correct historical billing where possible (CS-4821 escalation). I'll coordinate with billing ops.

devon (Oncall): Patch deployed to gw-7 canary at 09:28 UTC. Initial metrics: 5xx dropped ~82% for affected req patterns, client_abort label increased accordingly. Continuing rollout.

sara (Support): Awesome, marking as ongoing and updating CS ticket.
